nombre_oficial.texto: The Las Monjas Complex and Akab Dzib

frase_gancho.texto: Masks of the rain god and a government palace.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: In the south of the standard route stands the Las Monjas complex, a government palace that grew in at least six stages. There are four stops. First, the main building, with inscriptions that mention the ruler K'ak'upakal. Then the East Annex, with its facade of masks of Chaac, the rain god, and La Iglesia, a small temple with niches that are identified with the Bacabes, the gods who held up the sky. Nearby is the Akab Dzib, in the Puuc style, dated to around the year eight hundred sixty-nine. Its name means house of mysterious writing.
